SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

What should the agent do better next time?

Illustrative example · an agent reconciles a financial report, then receives a new company’s files.

Save the useful check

Check units and reporting periods.
Reconcile totals before writing.
Record when those checks apply.

See whether it helps again

New company: does the procedure help?
Different task: should it be retrieved?
Later updates: does it still work?

An agent learns from experience when a saved change improves what it does on later work.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

Learning new tasks also raises two different questions

The whole agent can learn through saved instructions, software changes, or model training.

Can it keep learning?

Learn a new task without losing
what worked on earlier tasks.

This is continual learning.

Can it learn to learn better?

Use experience to improve how
it learns the next task.

This is meta-learning.

These questions can overlap. A better learning method still needs to preserve earlier abilities.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

What can experience change?

A saved instruction can change the agent’s behavior even when the underlying model stays the same.

What changesConcrete exampleHow it helps later work
Notes or reusable skillsSave a checklist for checking a reportRead and apply it on the next report
Prompts or agent softwareChange when to call a tool or check an answerFollow a better procedure next time
Model weightsTrain on examples produced from experienceUse behavior learned through training

The agent’s “harness” is the software that organizes its model calls, tools, and task execution.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSRESULTS / USEFUL EXPERTISE

Can one mistake teach the agent a reusable check?

FinEvo example · the agent writes a financial report, receives feedback, and saves instructions for later reports.

A mistake in one report

The report says gross margin is 40.02%.
Its own revenue and cost imply 41.00%.
The judging model flags the error.

A check for the next report

Recompute the margin from revenue and cost.
Check the summary against the calculations.
Save these instructions; keep model weights fixed.

This documents a saved correction. Whether it prevents later mistakes needs a separate test.

Why learn the check if an expert could supply it?

01

Start fresh

Clear lessons between tasks. Each case starts without experience from earlier cases.

What can the agent do on its own?
02

Give good instructions

Supply an expert procedure before the work begins. Keep it fixed throughout.

What does good preparation buy?
03

Learn from feedback

After each case, revise reusable instructions for future cases.

What extra benefit does learning buy?

120 tasks, three shuffled orders. These are separate experimental conditions, not stages of one training run.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSRESULTS / DURABILITY

Does memory still help when the work changes?

AgentStream tests 300 tasks across six domains, including coding and web research. Model weights stay fixed.

Learning loop
Attempt a task → save notes or procedures → reuse them on later tasks.
Comparison
The same model, carrying no lessons between tasks.

Isolated · separate histories

Each domain learns from its own tasks. Lessons stay within that domain.

Sequential · shared history

Finish one domain, then start the next. Carry the saved lessons across.

Interleaved · shared history

Mix tasks from different domains. Keep learning into one shared history.

Updates use execution results and self-reflection; correct-answer labels are withheld from the learning agent.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSRESULTS / DURABILITY

SEAL’s earlier gains shrink as it learns more passages

Test 2 · Keep updating the same model on new passages, and re-test answers about earlier passages.

Follow the first column

Passage 0: 33% before learning → 38% just after learning it → 19% after all eight updates.

What changed?

Later passages triggered more weight updates. Answers about the first passage became less accurate.

Why SEAL belongs here

Learning new facts helped. Keeping those gains through further learning needed a separate test.

This SEAL recipe did not optimize retention. The result does not establish that all weight-update methods forget.

Can the agent improve how it proposes its next change?

So far, experience has changed instructions and training data. It might also improve the method used to propose future changes.

Hyperagents makes that method editable, then tests whether a developed system can improve on new work.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSRESULTS / IMPROVING THE IMPROVER

Hyperagents can edit the code that proposes improvements

The system contains a task-solving agent and a second agent that proposes changes to it.

Task-solving code

The code that performs the work can change.

Improvement code

The code that proposes edits can also change. This is the “meta-agent.”

Test and keep candidates

The experiment still fixes how candidates are selected and evaluated.

Being able to edit the improvement method does not establish that the new method is better.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSCONCLUSION

Learning is useful when a correction helps again

Our interpretation of the evidence: turn experience into checks that improve later work.

01

Add something useful

Compare learned instructions with good instructions supplied upfront.

FinEvo: 93.71 versus 86.67
02

Use it at the right time

Select relevant lessons and check that later learning preserves earlier abilities.

AgentStream and SEAL show why
03

Justify the added work

Count learning and operating costs, then ask what the better outcomes are worth.

More use alone does not ensure savings

A saved correction is a promising mechanism. Sustained improvements and economic value still need to be measured.

Test whether the correction changes what happens next time

Proposed evaluation · compare agents on the same new work

QuestionComparisonWhat to measure
Does experience help?Saved lessons vs reset vs expert instructionsQuality on the same new tasks
When does a lesson apply?Related tasks vs different kinds of workBenefit or harm from reusing it
What survives later learning?Revisit old tasks after new updatesEarlier skills retained or lost
Is learning worth its cost?Learning vs good instructions vs extra attemptsBetter outcomes and all added costs

Use repeated runs and independent evaluation. Test both saved changes and the ability to keep learning.

When would you choose to keep learning?

  1. 01

    Would the extra quality justify the extra work?

    FinEvo: fixed instructions score 86.67; learned procedures 93.71, using about 3.9× the recorded tokens.

  2. 02

    Which lesson should the agent use—or stop using?

    A saved check may be irrelevant, outdated, or lost during later learning. These need different remedies.

    What would convince you a correction lasts?
